newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares extend heady bull-run.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares extend heady bull-run.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares soared to new heights on Friday with brokers and market analysts saying the bulls had gone mad on the bourse on strong fundamentals.

The key 57-share industrial index rose 2.2 percent -- or 147.45 points, its highest ever gain in a single day -- to close at 6,897.15, a new record level. This was a surge of 398.05 points on the week.
"The mad bulls are still driving the exchange to new heights, and their condition seems to have become more contagious," said market analyst and columnist Charles Gurney.
"The growth in some counters is remarkable...and there appears to be no stopping the current momentum," Gurney said.
Another broker said: "There's bull madness on the market now because some of the prices people are paying now are ridiculous."
Brokers said the bull-run seemed to be gaining momentum rather than slowing down for a price correction.

"The fundamentals are looking strong, interest rates are no longer a sticky point because they are coming down. The only thing that might induce a price correction may be an upward trend in annual inflation in August," another broker told Reuters.

Annual inflation fell to 22 percent in July from 28 percent in January, leading the central Reserve Bank to cut by two percentage points its key rediscount rate to 27.5 percent, fuelling hopes of lower interest rates.

The bull-run also gained impetus last week after the Reserve Bank raised to 40 percent from 35 percent of total shares in a company listed on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange foreigners are allowed to own as part of efforts to boost foreign investment.

On the exchange on Friday, sugar refinery ZSR led the day's winners, rising 100 cents to 1,200, followed by 50-cent gains in farming implement-maker Zimplow at 300, cement producer Porthold at 1,250, clothing retailer Edgars at 2,950 and Alloys at 900.

Tobacco firm TSL climbed 45 cents to 470, finance group Finhold rose 40 cents to 790 while building company J and F at 195, pork processor Colcom at 300 and cable manufacturer BICAF at 425 all jumped 25 cents up.

Clothing retailer Truworths at 770, sugar producer Hippo at 820 and retailers Haddon and Sly at 300 all gained 20 cents while 15-cent rises were posted in textiler Spinweave at 140, packaging firm Hunyani at 310 and food group Cairns at 815.
Minings also closed firmer and active, with gold producer Falcon leaping 150 cents to 1,750, Falgold firming five cents to 185 and nickel company Bindura rising 50 cents to 1,250.
The seven-counter mining index put on 4.52 points to 1,414.21 -- a jump of 93.44 points on the week.
